Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Depressive symptoms decreased after the Nordic Walking program with vitamin D supplementation in elderly women.
Sentence: "The study also showed a decrease in depressive symptoms (p = 0.026)."
Measured as: severity of depressive symptoms (Beck Depression Inventory 2)
Population: 52 healthy elderly women in Poland
Intervention: Nordic Walking training program plus vitamin D supplementation
Comparator: none (single-arm, before vs after)
Design: case series
Sample size: 52
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: harm
Claim: In PD patients given vitamin D3, folic acid and B12 for 6 months, the 15D depression dimension score significantly increased (improved) from baseline.
Sentence: "After the intervention, the mean score of speech, mental function, discomfort and symptoms, depression, and QoL significantly increased (p < 0.05 for all)."
Measured as: depression (15D dimension score)
Population: Levodopa-treated Parkinson's disease patients in Romania, mean age 71 years
Intervention: Daily tablet with 800 IU vitamin D3, 1000 µg folic acid, 15 µg vitamin B12 for 6 months
Comparator: None (single-arm, baseline vs 6 months)
Design: case series
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Responses

### Response A

```json
 "rationale": "Study B’s increased 15D depression score indicates improvement, not harm, and measures a quality-of-life dimension rather than the full depressive-symptom scale used in Study A.",

  "population",
  "intervention"
 ],
 "detail": "15D depression dimension versus Beck Depression Inventory II; both reported changes indicate improvement."
}
```
